concerns.text: Tasks T012c, T012e, and T012e2 mandate generating and committing static test fixtures (e.g., 'real_ground_truth_proxy.json') derived from external datasets. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility), which requires that 'Every result... MUST be reproducible by re-running the project's code/ against the project's data/ on a fresh GitHub Actions runner' and that 'External datasets MUST be fetched... on every run.' Pre-generating derived data as static artifacts creates a 'hand-typed' dependency that breaks the reproducibility loop.

Task T035s ('Simulated Gold Standard Generation') creates a deterministic file with 'randomly assigned' labels to enable CI testing. This directly violates Constitution Principle VI (Zero-Shot Drift Detection Validity), which mandates validation against a 'human-annotated gold standard' with 'Kappa > 0.6'. Relying on random simulation for the validation logic undermines the core scientific claim that the Drift Score predicts emergent threats, as the 'gold standard' is synthetic noise rather than human judgment.

The Spec (US-03) explicitly requires a baseline comparison against 'gpto-mini'. The tasks (T039-series) unilaterally substitute 'google/flan-t5-small' due to 'memory constraints' without a formal scope change approval or justification in the spec. This is a silent relaxation of the Spec's acceptance criteria (which assumes the specified LLM baseline) and violates the Single Source of Truth principle (Constitution Principle IV) by altering the experimental design without traceability.

Task T012a-timestamp-handling generates 'deterministic placeholder timestamps' for records missing this field. The Spec (Data Model) defines 'timestamp' as a required field. Generating synthetic timestamps for input data violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle III (Data Hygiene) by introducing non-canonical, derived data into the input stream, potentially invalidating the statistical validation (p < 0.05) required by US-01 if the timestamp distribution affects the drift calculation.
